confirmed: Criterion 3 holds. S1-O1 is computed on every story: 'All stories were scored for their originality using the Multilingual Assessment of Short Stories (MAoSS) model', a fine-tuned LLM trained to predict human-rated originality (r = .86 with human ratings of English stories). It is not a self-report (p. 11, Method, Scoring, Originality).

S1-O2 is computed on the stories. The paper takes sentence embeddings from paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 (final layer 12), removes the prompt words, and averages the 1 - cosine distance over all story pairs in each prompt dataset. Each story's score is that dataset diversity minus the diversity with the story removed (pp. 11-12, Method, Scoring, Diversity Contribution; Figure 1, p. 13).

AI availability holds for S1-O1 and S1-O2. In AI-help, 'participants were instructed to collaborate with ChatGPT during the story writing task'. In No-AI, the ChatGPT textbox was removed. Both stories were scored as written in the online study, so yes and immediate fit (p. 9, Procedure; p. 10, Story Writing Task; Appendices A and B, p. 32).

Question codes follow the codebook rule. S1-O1 (originality, AI available) is with_ai, and S1-O2 (diversity, AI available) is across_people. The paper reports no analysis by order and no unassisted outcome after an AI phase, so no after_ai outcome is missing. The form flags the carryover in open_questions (codebook Section 1; form-spec field note 'question'; pp. 14-18).

Construct novelty fits S1-O1: the paper's term is originality, scored on a 0-1 scale. Construct diversity fits S1-O2. Pairs are formed only within the two prompt datasets ('leading to 2 different datasets'), and the prompts were counterbalanced across conditions, with one prompt 'given to that participant for the AI-help condition'. So each dataset holds one story per participant, and every pair joins two different people (p. 9, Story Writing Task; pp. 11-12; p. 18 for the scale).
Measure codes fit: automated_score for MAoSS (a language model used as a scorer) and embedding_similarity for the cosine-distance contribution (codebook Section 6; p. 11).

Unit participant fits S1-O1 and S1-O2. Both are paired-samples t-tests with t(262) on the 263 analyzed participants. The printed d values equal t / sqrt(263) (5.56 / 16.22 = .343; 1.99 / 16.22 = .123), as expected for 263 participant-level difference scores (p. 9, Participants; p. 14; p. 17).

S1-O1 numbers match the PDF exactly: AI-help M = .56, SD = 08 vs No-AI M = .52, SD = 08; t(262) = 5.56, p < .001, d = .34, 95% CI [.021, .045]. The 'SD = 08' typo is in both the page image and the text layer (p. 14, Results, Story Originality; Figure 2, left panel, p. 15).

S1-O2 numbers match exactly: AI-help M = -.000026, SD = .00033 vs No-AI M = .000027, SD = .00034; t(262) = -1.99, p = .047, d = -.123, 95% CI [-0.0001, -0.0000006]. 'Positive scores indicated that removing the story decreased diversity', so higher = more diverse, and treatment_lower needs no sign reversal. The Figure 2 note says the plotted values are multiplied by 10^3 (p. 12; p. 15; p. 17, Results, Story Diversity).
Primary codes hold: 'We thus investigated two main outcomes of story originality and diversity'. Self-assessment accuracy is introduced as a further question (p. 8, The Present Research).

S1-O3 is a self-report: 1-5 Likert self-ratings of each story's originality, collected 'At the end of the main-story task'. So scored_on_output false, measure self_report, and question none fit the form spec ('Use none for outcomes that answer none of the three'). This is also the most common coding of self_report outcomes in the final forms (11 of 21, this one included). Its numbers match: tau .161 [.078, .244] and .195 [.112, .278]; t(413) = -0.22, p = .83, b = -0.001; error 2.43 (SD 1.15) vs 2.14 (SD 1.18). Unit output fits the multilevel model, where self-assessments are nested in participants (p. 11, Self-Assessment; pp. 17-18, Self-Assessment Accuracy).

No outcome is missing. No AI-help vs No-AI contrast on word count is printed: word-count difference scores enter only as controls in partial correlations. Integration of AI responses and prompt counts exist only in the AI-help arm and enter only correlations (Figure 3, Appendix D). The classical creativity tasks preceded the story task and are not analyzed (p. 9, Procedure; p. 12; pp. 14-17; p. 34).

Comparison type ai_vs_bau fits. Telling No-AI writers to pose the practice prompting strategies to themselves is not an aid such as search, examples, or a partner (p. 11, practice paragraph; codebook Section 5).

Side note outside the outcome lens: the markdown on disk was written 2026-10-04 21:26, before the form, and holds the full paper through the Conclusions, References, and Appendix D. The form's note that it 'stops partway through the Discussion (PDF p. 22)' is out of date. No outcome field depends on it. All 34 PDF pages were read as page images, and every number above was also matched in the text layer (md file, sections 'Conclusions' and 'Appendix D').
summary: All three c159 outcomes are coded correctly: MAoSS originality (S1-O1) and the leave-one-out embedding diversity contribution (S1-O2) are computed on the stories that participants wrote, with ChatGPT available in the AI-help arm, and their question, construct, measure, unit (participant, paired t-tests with df = 262), and printed numbers match the PDF (pp. 11-17), so criterion 3 holds. S1-O3 is correctly kept as a self-report that answers none of the three questions, no outcome is missing, and the one real caveat (diversity contribution is measured against a pool that mixes both arms) is already disclosed in diversity_detail and open_questions.
